blocks.text: If the gateway crashes before delivery, the pending row survives and is found after restart. If delivery succeeds but recording completion fails, the row remains pending and is retried. These two cases share the same recovery action because worker-side deduplication makes replay meaningful.

topics.title: 18.3.1 Walking the Failure Matrix
topics.summary: Before the gateway commit, no accepted obligation exists. After gateway commit but before worker commit, the gateway retains pending work. After worker commit but before a received reply, the worker retains a replayable result. After a received reply but before gateway completion commit, the gateway may retry and obtain that same result. After gateway completion commit, status can return done.

cards.question: Explain Walking the Failure Matrix in your own words.
cards.answer: Before the gateway commit, no accepted obligation exists. After gateway commit but before worker commit, the gateway retains pending work. After worker commit but before a received reply, the worker retains a replayable result. After a received reply but before gateway completion commit, the gateway may retry and obtain that same result. After gateway completion commit, status can return done.

blocks.text: 18.3.1 Walking the Failure Matrix

blocks.text: Before the gateway commit, no accepted obligation exists. After gateway commit but before worker commit, the gateway retains pending work. After worker commit but before a received reply, the worker retains a replayable result. After a received reply but before gateway completion commit, the gateway may retry and obtain that same result. After gateway completion commit, status can return done.

blocks.text: This sequence is the central recovery argument. Each gap has durable state on at least the relevant side and a defined action. It does not require both databases to commit simultaneously, but it does require their independent state not to be casually discarded.

blocks.text: A partial disaster restore can violate the argument. Restoring an old worker database may remove receipts for effects already reported by the gateway. Restoring an old gateway may remove pending jobs or completed status records. Recovery must reconcile authorities and any real external effects before reopening ordinary traffic.

blocks.text: The integration suite includes a worker mode that commits its first valid operation and then drops the reply deliberately. The gateway must retry, complete the job, and leave exactly one receipt. The failpoint is placed after commit specifically to test the ambiguous outcome, not merely an easy failure before work begins.

reading.title: 18.3.1 Walking the Failure Matrix
paragraphs: Before the gateway commit, no accepted obligation exists. After gateway commit but before worker commit, the gateway retains pending work. After worker commit but before a received reply, the worker retains a replayable result. After a received reply but before gateway completion commit, the gateway may retry and obtain that same result. After gateway completion commit, status can return done.

This sequence is the central recovery argument. Each gap has durable state on at least the relevant side and a defined action. It does not require both databases to commit simultaneously, but it does require their independent state not to be casually discarded.

A partial disaster restore can violate the argument. Restoring an old worker database may remove receipts for effects already reported by the gateway. Restoring an old gateway may remove pending jobs or completed status records. Recovery must reconcile authorities and any real external effects before reopening ordinary traffic.

The failpoint is placed after commit specifically to test the ambiguous outcome, not merely an easy failure before work begins.
